Every engineer on the team owns a system or a set of subsystems from start to finish. Your scope here grows with your experience and the ownership you show. This is a rare chance to write the fundamental design of something new, for a mission of national importance. jobs.title: Summer 2027 Internship - Information Security Engineer
jobs.description_text: About This Role General Matter builds its own technology: the software, firmware, control systems, and infrastructure that run an industrial nuclear fuel facility. At most companies, a security bug costs you data. Here, the software we build, and any security vulnerabilities we miss, touch the real world. The Security team's job is to find those gaps before anyone else does. We do that through offensive testing, code audits, design reviews, and hardening the systems we ship. As an intern on the team, you'll attack General Matter's products and infrastructure, while working with the engineers who own them to fix what you find. Targets include web apps, APIs, Linux and Windows hosts, cloud environments, embedded devices, and industrial controllers. You'll own real projects from start to finish, and you won't be writing policy documents Responsibilities Break everything you touch, then help us fix it. Run penetration tests against General Matter networks, services, web applications, and APIs. Prove what you find with working proof-of-concept exploits. Audit source code and features for security vulnerabilities in languages like Python, C, C++, Rust, Go, and TypeScript. Then build static analysis rules or CI checks so the same class of bug can't come back. Reverse engineer and attack embedded devices and industrial equipment on an isolated test bench.
